decisions.reason: The source reiterates that the accent must reuse the exact Hero V terminal geometry, but the candidate already requires a literal terminal derivation and exact one-to-one vector match. No candidate state change is needed.
The request for three new E and L concepts does not change the established second-V height hierarchy or visual role.
The Hero V remains the established reference language and is described as being back where it belongs; the source changes exploration of the E and L forms, not the Hero V geometry.
The source repeats the literal accent-derivation rule but does not change or contradict the existing requirement that the Hero V and accent peaks align exactly.
Exploring more original E and L forms does not alter the second V's derivation rule or right-arm geometry.

The exact-copy instruction applies specifically to the É accent and is already represented by the accent-derivation requirement; it does not change the shared terminal treatment across all three V-system elements.
The source requests distinct architectural E and L concepts but does not modify spacing, kerning, or the unified-reading goal.
The E and L exploration request contains no decision about color, material treatment, or resuming the deferred champagne-metal work.
Requesting three genuinely different architectural concepts does not change the separate obligation to include a brief design rationale with each review round.
The source contains no decision about attachment formats or proof accessibility.
